title: Jefferies Gets New Evidence of Fake Invoices at Beleaguered Fund
summary: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. has been told that some of the invoices underpinning its financing to an iron ore trader called Sapphire Minmetals Corp. are not genuine, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: OPEC Output Rose in July Led by Gulf Nations, Survey Shows
summary: OPEC’s crude oil production recouped some more of its wartime losses last month with gains in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Iraq, though opaque shipping data complicated the process of tracking the group’s output, a Bloomberg survey showed.

title: AbbVie Set to Sell $10 Billion in Bonds to Fund Apogee Deal
summary: AbbVie Inc. has launched a $10 billion investment-grade bond sale to help fund its pending acquisition of fellow drugmaker Apogee Therapeutics Inc.

title: Europe's Key Rivers are Drying Up As Extreme Heat Impact Widens
summary: Europe’s biggest rivers are drying up after a series of heat waves. That’s disrupting the transport of goods and curbing power generation across the continent, Rachel Graham explains (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Novo Nordisk Slides as Forecast Boost Fails to Impress
summary: Novo Nordisk A/S raised its forecasts for the second time this year, citing higher expectations for its obesity and diabetes drug sales, though the magnitude of the increase failed to impress investors.

title: Griffin’s NYC Office Tower Set to Land $3.3 Billion Construction Loan
summary: The team working on Citadel’s new Manhattan skyscraper expects to secure a $3.3 billion construction loan for the project.

title: McDonald’s Replaces US Boss After Slowest Growth in Over a Year
summary: McDonald’s Corp. named a new US president to bring “focus and urgency” to its home market, after the fast-food chain posted its slowest growth in over a year. Bloomberg's Michael Halen joins to discuss this as well as how Taco Bell's parent company, Yum! Brands, was in touch with Michigan health authorities about a parasitic outbreak in early July, weeks before the company officially alerted consumers. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 4

title: El problema del yen ya preocupa también a Estados Unidos

title: Hellman & Friedman’s Baker Tilly Calls Off $3 Billion Debt Deal
summary: Baker Tilly has dropped plans for a roughly $3 billion leveraged loan that was intended to refinance private credit debt and fund a dividend, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Treasuries Rise as Falling Oil Prices Ease Pressure on Fed
summary: Treasuries rose on Tuesday as signs of progress toward a diplomatic resolution of the Iran war sent oil prices lower, curbing expectations for more than one Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in the coming year.

title: European Stocks Close at Record on Upbeat Earnings, Mining Rally
summary: European stocks hit a record high, boosted by another strong set of earnings, a rally in mining shares and optimism that a Middle East truce will be reached soon.

title: SpaceX Is Wall Street’s Frothiest Trade: Sloan
summary: Short-sellers are making a massive bet against SpaceX. Bob Sloan S3 Partners Founder & Managing Partner calls it one of the frothiest trades the market has ever seen. He joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why bears are already billions of dollars ahead, what could trigger a short squeeze, and whether the broader market is finally losing its speculative excess. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Trade Is In ‘Kindness of Strangers’ Phase, Says One CIO

title: Crop Trader ADM Raises 2026 Outlook as Biofuels Drive Growth
